title: Permutation-Preserving Truncation of Cycle Walking
summary: A naive cutoff can fail to produce a unique target-set image; whether bounded-step cycle walking can still define a target-set permutation remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For a target subset $S \subseteq T$ and a permutation $\pi:T\to T$ of the ambient set $T$, determine whether there exists a bounded-step truncation of ordinary cycle walking $\mathrm{CW}_{\pi}$ on $S$ that maps every $x\in S$ to a unique point of $S$ and defines a permutation of $S$. The obstacle is that a naive cutoff may occur while the walk is traversing $T\setminus S$, leaving no unique point in $S$ to serve as the image of $x$.

scope.domain: Ordinary cycle walking for target-set permutation construction in symmetric cryptography.
assumptions: S is a target subset of T.
π is a permutation of T.
parameters: S: target set on which the truncated walk must define a permutation
T: ambient set traversed by ordinary cycle walking
π: permutation of T used by ordinary cycle walking
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a bounded-step truncation of ordinary cycle walking can map every point of S to a unique point of S and thereby define a permutation of S.

citations.label: Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications

progress.summary: The source explains that a naive cutoff may stop while the walk is outside the target subset and thus fail to supply a unique target image. It introduces reverse cycle walking as an alternative, leaving truncation of ordinary cycle walking unresolved.
citation_labels: Sarah Miracle et al., Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications
